topSignals.title: Oracle publicly reaffirms 2.4 GW Bloom Energy fuel-cell contract for Project Jupiter; BE stock jumps 8%.
topSignals.text: Following Sept 24's force-majeure notice, Oracle, developer Blue Owl Capital, and Bloom Energy all stated on Sept 25 that the New Mexico data-center fuel-cell deal remains intact and on Oracle's planned timeline. Bloom (BE) rose ~8% to $288.77 (232% YTD). Analysts note the force-majeure filing itself signals real schedule risk was worth legally shielding against: the site's gas-pipeline permit and the fuel-cell installation's air-quality permit are both still pending New Mexico approval. 24/7 Wall St., Fuel Cells Works

topSignals.title: Priority stack check — Elcogen active on testing/QA infrastructure, Topsoe quiet.
topSignals.text: Elcogen signed a multi-year cooperation with Estonian testing/metrology body Metrosert on Sept 21 to expand solid-oxide stack testing capacity, and published a SOEC whitepaper on Sept 23 — both signal continued institutional build-out rather than a product or capacity announcement. Topsoe posted no SOFC/SOEC news in the last 24-48h; its most recent substantive news remains the earlier 2026 SOEC-pathway guidance cut and H1 results. Elcogen News, Topsoe Press Releases

topSignals.title: Germany's EEG-Novelle/Netzpaket clears Bundestag first reading, hits Bundesrat friction on Sept 25.
topSignals.text: The Bundesrat voted on ~120 pages of committee amendments (small-PV feed-in-tariff protections, a contested "Redispatch-Vorbehalt" grid-curtailment clause that Schleswig-Holstein's energy minister called "completely wrong and toxic"), but the specific vote outcome was not published by the Sept 25 evening deadline. Full passage is still needed in October to meet the EU deadline — relevant for any German behind-the-meter/islanded SOFC generation model. pv magazine

items.text: Elcogen (priority): Sept 21 — multi-year testing cooperation with Metrosert to strengthen SOFC/SOEC stack testing. Sept 23 — released whitepaper "The Case for Solid Oxide Electrolysis Technology." No new capacity or product-launch news in the window. Elcogen News
Topsoe (priority): Quiet — no SOFC/SOEC, capacity, or partnership news dated to the last 24-48h found on Topsoe's own press page or in search. Topsoe Press Releases

Bloom Energy, FuelCell Energy, Ceres Power, Sunfire, SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera, Aisin: no new stack/cell-technology announcements (as opposed to commercial/financial news, covered below) found in the last 24-48h.

Top story — see Top Signal #3:* Germany's EEG-Novelle/Netzpaket Bundesrat committee vote on Sept 25; outcome not yet published, October passage still needed for the EU deadline. Standing US background unchanged since yesterday's digest: FERC's June 2026 show-cause order to PJM/MISO/SPP/CAISO/ISO-NE/NYISO on interconnection queue reform and fast-track fuel-cell/data-center co-location compliance steps; ITC 48E 30% fuel-cell credit and 45V hydrogen credit unchanged post-OBBBA; Virginia self-generation tax, New York permit moratorium, Texas development pause, EPA turbine NSPS all as previously logged — no new developments on these in the last 24-48h.
Bloom Energy (BE): +8% on Sept 25 to $288.77 on the Oracle reaffirmation — see Top Signal #1. Q3 earnings still due Oct 27; scandium securities-suit lead-plaintiff deadline Sept 28.

FuelCell Energy (FCEL): No new operational disclosures; additional plaintiff-firm reminder press releases continue ahead of the Nov 10, 2026 lead-plaintiff deadline (Fit Energy cost-overrun disclosure). Backlog remains $3.6B per the Q3 transcript.
Ceres Power (CWR.L): No new market-moving news since the Sept 23 H1 results already logged in prior digests.

lcoe.text: New Henry Hub actual-price datapoint (published Sept 25, EIA Today in Energy): Summer 2026 (Jun-Aug) Henry Hub spot averaged $2.93/MMBtu, 6% below summer 2025 — notably lower than the carried August STEO full-year-2026 forecast average of ~$3.43-3.44/MMBtu, and well below the LCOE model's carried $4.00-4.30/MMBtu assumption. EIA's September STEO separately projects record 2026 dry gas production of 111.2 Bcf/d and end-October storage ~5% above the five-year average — directionally bearish for gas prices into Q4, worth reconciling against the model's fuel-cost assumption. EIA Today in Energy

Permitting-timeline datapoint (qualitative, carried from Top Signal #1): Project Jupiter's fuel-cell air-quality permit and gas-pipeline permit remain pending in New Mexico — a live, dated illustration of permitting/interconnection lead-time risk to weigh against SOFC's "~90-day build" framing when modeling deployment schedules.

Pending calendar: Bloom lead-plaintiff deadline (Sept 28), PJM backstop bid window (Sept 30-Oct 21), FCEL lead-plaintiff deadline (Nov 10), New Mexico air-quality permit deadline for Project Jupiter (Nov 23), Bloom Q3 earnings (Oct 27), EEG-Novelle/Netzpaket targeted for October passage.
